From: Finometrics DevOps <ops@finometrics.com>

Date: Fri, 19 Jan 2028 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Tokenization latency spike affecting embed pipeline

Hello Jordan,

We observed a sharp increase in tokenization latency starting ~13:50 PST that impacted batched embedding requests across our account. Latency climbed from ~35ms/token to ~380ms/token for a 20-minute window. This caused downstream timeouts in our ingestion pipeline and multiple failed jobs.

We attached a short trace and logs for the timeframe (tokenization_trace.log). Can you confirm whether this was a customer-side input pattern or a platform-side issue? We need a short briefing for our incident review later today.

Thanks,
Susan Park
Head of Data Engineering
Finometrics

--

Plan:

- Marissa and Karthik will reproduce locally against the trace and provide a short timeline.
- We'll return a customer-facing RCA with timeline and actions within 48 hours.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll prioritize this.

Date: Sat, 20 Jan 2028 09:04:22 -0800
Subject: Internal: initial findings on tokenization latency

Team — quick internal notes after reproducing against the customer's trace.

Findings (summary):
- Trigger: a small set (~12) of requests used a long-form document (token count > 60k) that pushed the tokenizer into a slow fallback code path when encountering a rare Unicode cluster sequence.
- Impact window: 13:49:52 - 14:09:30 PST (approx).
- Root cause: a recently merged micro-optimization to the tokenizer indexing logic didn't handle a specific combining sequence; under high token-count batches this caused repeated rescans and fallback to a slower algorithm.
- Contributing factor: the serving runtime selected a conservative kernel variant for those sequences due to a short-lived kernel compatibility probe; that increased per-token latency for the impacted requests.

Immediate mitigations applied (20 Jan 03:15 UTC):
1) Reverted the micro-optimization on the tokenizer indexing in Canary to prevent the fallback path.
2) Forced a kernel pin for the affected model variant on the serving fleet to avoid the conservative fallback.
3) Applied a short-term prefix caching override for the customer's account to reduce repeated token scans.

Next actions (owner, target):
- Marissa: produce a short RCA slide pack and logs extraction for customer delivery (ASAP, Target: 22 Jan 09:00 PST).
- Karthik: add a unit test for the Unicode cluster case and block the micro-optimization until verified in regression suite (Target: patch in 48 hours).
- Grace: proposal for operational guardrail — monitor token-count distribution and auto-throttle long sequences by default (Target: design doc by 02 Feb).

Attachments: rca-summary-slides.pdf (draft), mitigation-checklist.csv

Marissa Cole
Sr. Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 22 Jan 2028 09:42:11 -0800
Subject: Final RCA and corrective plan — tokenization latency anomaly (summary)

Hi Susan — thank you again for reporting the issue and for the trace; below is the customer-facing RCA, timeline, and action items. We appreciate your patience.

Executive summary:
- What happened: On 2028-01-19 between ~13:50 and 14:10 PST, certain batched embedding requests for Finometrics experienced elevated tokenization latency due to a combination of (1) a tokenizer micro-optimization that missed a rare Unicode cluster case and (2) the serving runtime selecting a conservative kernel variant for those requests.
- Impact: increased per-token latency (35ms -> ~380ms) for a 20-minute window; several ingestion jobs timed out. No customer data was exposed.

Timeline (brief):
- 13:50 PST — first customer errors and elevated latency observed.
- 13:52 PST — Finometrics sent trace to Redwood.
- 14:10 PST — initial mitigation attempt (kernel pin) reduced tail latency.
- 03:15 UTC (20 Jan) — tokenizer micro-optimization reverted in Canary; prefix caching override applied for Finometrics.
- 09:00 PST (22 Jan) — final mitigations confirmed and fixes scheduled for release.

Root cause: A code change in the tokenizer optimization path failed to handle a rare combining Unicode sequence present in a small subset of very long documents, causing the tokenizer to enter a slow fallback loop. Concurrently, serving runtime behavior selected a conservative kernel variant for those request signatures, amplifying the latency impact.

Actions completed for Finometrics:
- Immediate rollback of the tokenizer micro-optimization in Canary.
- Kernel pin forced for the affected model variant on the serving fleet handling Finometrics traffic.
- Account-level prefix caching override applied to reduce repeated rescans during ingestion.

Planned fixes and timeline:
- Karthik to ship a guarded tokenizer patch with a regression test for the Unicode cluster case (ETA: 48 hours).
- Operational guardrail to monitor and auto-throttle extremely long sequences in the next quarter; design doc by 02 Feb (Grace).
- Post-release verification run and replay of your supplied trace across fleet (we will share verification logs).

Compensation and goodwill: we recognize the operational impact. I'll loop our account execs separately to propose a credits package for the impacted jobs.

Attachments: rca-summary-slides.pdf (final), mitigation-checklist.csv, tokenization_trace.log (customer-provided)

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough this week with Marissa and Karthik to go over the trace and the patch plan. Please let me know a time that works.

Regards,
